Act 46 (2024) reduced income taxes for most people in Hawaiʻi, although wealthier taxpayers benefited the most. These tax cuts would have eventually cost the state $1.45 billion every year by 2031.[^cor-forecast] This path was not sustainable: it would have led to severe cuts to the budget that would have directly affected people who rely on programs such as SNAP and Medicaid.

With Act 24 in 2026, the Legislature decided to keep some of these tax cuts for low- to middle-income residents, while raising taxes on people earning over $1 million. However, these changes will not compensate for the entire shortfall, and Hawaiʻi also needs to prepare itself for federal spending cuts. In order to do that, the state must consider all the tools it has at its disposal.
